Hello, friends. I’m Chen, a veteran trader with ten years of experience in the markets.
In my early years, I first ventured into the physical business world. I traveled the ups and downs of foreign trade, worked hard in real-world malls for many years, and truly tasted the cold and warmth of entrepreneurship.

I’ve had moments of glory—orders surging and profits soaring—but I’ve also faced the harsh winters of the market, huge losses, and those darkest periods when money was hard to circulate.

My offline business was always fluctuating, so I started getting involved in trading. I originally intended to use trading as a side venture to hedge risks.

But little did I expect that in the first few years after I entered the market, I traded purely on impulse and intuition.

I chased rallies and cut losses too frequently, took heavy positions to bet on the market’s direction. I had no rules, didn’t understand risk management, and the savings I built up through offline struggle kept shrinking again and again in the market.

Profits were always brief and elusive, but losses kept coming one after another. The hard-earned money from my offline business—on several occasions—was given back dramatically through trading.

Offline entrepreneurship trained my perspective, while setbacks in trading磨练了 my temperament.

Over ten years, I’ve been reviewing business logic while refining my trading approach.
I slowly saw through the essence of how business and the market are connected: long-term stability matters far more than getting rich overnight.

I kicked the restless, gambler mindset. I built a complete, mature, trading system tailored to current market conditions, and integrated risk-control thinking from business into how I execute trades.

Along the way, I’ve endured the tug-of-war between profit and loss, the ups and downs, and I’ve made it through countless low points filled with self-doubt. Now, everything has finally landed firmly—I’ve achieved financial freedom.
From here on, I will continue sharing all the traps I’ve stepped on through years of real trading, the stable logic I’ve accumulated, and my risk-management insights.

I deeply understand how hard losses and anxiety can be to endure. I hope that every person who is currently lost and suffering losses can take fewer detours, let go of impatience, and slowly find the long-term stable path that belongs to you.

title: Grayscale Urges Senate to Pass the CLARITY Act: A Turning Point for U.S. Crypto Regulation
subTitle:
$BTC $EUL $ETH 
#grayscaleurgessenatevoteonclarityact 
The U.S. crypto industry may be approaching one of its most significant regulatory moments yet. Digital asset investment giant Grayscale has publicly called on the U.S. Senate to pass the CLARITY Act, arguing that clear rules are essential for innovation, investor protection, and America's leadership in blockchain technology.
The appeal comes as lawmakers continue debating how cryptocurrencies should be regulated, with uncertainty remaining one of the industry's biggest challenges.
Why Grayscale Supports the CLARITY Act
According to Grayscale, the current U.S. regulatory framework creates confusion for crypto companies, investors, and developers. Different agencies often take different approaches, making compliance difficult and slowing innovation.
The company believes the CLARITY Act would:
Define which digital assets are securities and which are commodities.Establish clearer responsibilities for U.S. regulators.Improve consumer and investor protections.Encourage blockchain innovation within the United States.Reduce legal uncertainty for crypto businesses.
Grayscale argues that a transparent regulatory framework would help responsible companies grow while increasing confidence among institutional and retail investors.
Potential Market Impact
If the Senate approves the legislation, the crypto market could benefit from:
Greater institutional participation.Increased regulatory certainty.More investment in blockchain startups.Stronger long-term market confidence.Improved competitiveness for the U.S. digital asset industry.
While regulation can sometimes create short-term volatility, many analysts believe that clear rules are ultimately positive for the industry's long-term growth.
Why Investors Are Watching
Regulatory developments have become one of the biggest catalysts for cryptocurrency prices. Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other digital assets often react sharply to major policy announcements.
A successful vote on the CLARITY Act could be viewed as a milestone toward mainstream crypto adoption in the United States. However, investors should remember that the legislative process can take time, and amendments or delays remain possible.
Grayscale's support for the CLARITY Act highlights the crypto industry's growing demand for clear, consistent regulation rather than regulatory uncertainty. Whether the Senate ultimately approves the bill or not, the debate represents another important step in shaping the future of digital assets in the United States.
For crypto investors, keeping a close eye on U.S. regulatory developments may be just as important as monitoring market trends, as policy decisions increasingly influence the direction of the digital asset ecosystem.

The U.S. military warns Trump that Iran is brewing a retaliatory operation; global risk assets are facing selling pressure, with BTC and ETH hit first.

In the medium term, if the conflict really drags on, market liquidity will keep tightening. My take

My view is very clear: bearish in the short term—don’t rush to catch falling knives.

山寨那边CATE、CASHCAT这种猫猫狗狗又冒出来了，这种盘子我建议看看就好，一天涨跌几十个点，赌性太重。ONDO和GRVT倒是有点想像空间，但成交量都不够大，合约深度太薄，插针能把你止损都扫掉。资金费率那边几个主流都是0.01%上下，还算健康，没到过热或者极度悲观的程度。

现在这个位置我的想法很简单，BTC稳住62,300以上就拿着多单，跌破就认怂。ETH在1,823的支撑也没破，可以跟着BTC联动做。但记住一点，恐慌指数27不是说马上反转，而是说该控制仓位了。留子弹，等确认信号，稳健点才能活得更久。别想着一夜暴富，先想着别爆仓。

$ETH 1878, the bounce is even higher, but the problem is getting bigger.

From 1820 to 1884, it bounced more than sixty points, and it looked like it might be reversing. But if you watch the flow of funds, you know that’s not right: for three hours the spot trading capital was continuously negative for twelve candles—none of them flipped. Money kept being pulled out; the bounce didn’t stop even after more than sixty points.

Earlier we said it bounced—then what? Now it bounces even higher—then what? It’s still the same: the more it bounces, the more sell orders there are.

The order book is frighteningly thin on the bid side. The sell side is about 20% thicker than the buy side. The bids are just a thin layer—once you hit, it pierces through. People who borrowed to go long have doubled during this period. The long-to-short ratio is 10 to 1; it’s stuffed in like it’s free money. The problem is that the price can’t be held: it was ground from 1927 down to 1820. Every bounce came with someone selling. Now that it’s bouncing back, it’s the same— the higher it bounces, the thicker the sell wall becomes, like unloading shares onto people.

The trade volume is getting smaller as it bounces. The candle at 10 o’clock still had about 17,000 in volume; later it dropped to only a little over 4,000—no one is following. Previously, during the bounce, the volume could still expand. This time, when it bounced up to 1884, the volume was almost half of the first time, which shows that the following crowd is getting smaller. Even the whale accounts’ long-to-short ratio is falling: in seven hours it dropped by more than a dozen percentage points, and big money is withdrawing.

Above, from 1884 to 1936 to 1982, it’s one layer pressing another. When it bounces up, nobody catches it. But when it falls, it drops fast. I can’t figure out where the buy-the-dip money inside is coming from.

#eth $ETH

content:
$ETH 1878，弹得更高了，问题也更大了。

从1820弹到1884，弹了六十多块，看着像要反转了。但盯一下资金流向就知道不对，三小时现货资金连续十二根全负，一根都没翻过来，钱一直在往外抽，弹了六十多块也没停过。之前说弹了然后呢，现在弹得更高了，然后呢？还是一样，卖盘越弹越多。

盘口买盘薄得吓人，卖盘比买盘多两成，买盘就那么薄薄一层，一砸就穿。借钱做多的人这段时间翻了一倍，多空比十比一，塞得跟不要钱一样。问题是价焊不住，从1927磨到1820，弹一次有人卖一次，现在弹回来还是一样，弹得越高卖盘越厚，越像给人出货。

成交越弹越小，十点那根还有一万七的量，到后面只剩四千多，没人跟了。之前弹的时候量还能放大，这次弹到1884量比第一次弹小了快一半，说明跟风盘越来越少。鲸鱼账户的多空比也在掉，七个钟头降了十几个点，大资金在撤。

上面从1884到1936到1982，一层压一层，弹上去没人接，下来倒是快得很。搞不明白，里面接盘的钱到底从哪来。

#baby $BABY A few days ago, when I had nothing to do in the middle of the night, I went over to the Aave V4 testnet just to wander around. I wanted to experience the native “no custodians, no cross-chain bridge” Bitcoin-backed lending. In the end, it took me three hours. I couldn’t help but complain in the developer group: “The big pie is indeed stable and hasn’t moved on the mainnet, but the U I posted as collateral really was nowhere to be seen.” @babylonlabs_io 

To be fair, the underlying architecture is pretty clever. The idea is to have everyone lock $BTC into the Taproot UTXO script on the mainnet. On the Ethereum side, it synchronously mints a 1:1 ERC-20 shadow asset—vaultBTC. You can then cash it out on the Aave market. When you repay, it generates a ZK proof, and once you throw it back on the original chain for verification, you can unlock. This kind of “remote bullseye” mechanism is exactly the sort of thing the market loves—no wonder Babylon is gaining serious momentum. The protocol’s TVL hit a peak of 72,000 BTC (about $4 billion), and cumulative activations exceed 100,000 BTC.

But no matter how good the story sounds on paper, the real-world execution is disappointing. I tried with 0.1 BTC. After locking, I stared at the screen for nearly twenty minutes before the frontend finally, slowly, showed the vaultBTC balance. The crux of the issue is node synchronization. Babylon has to be honest and wait for the mainnet to produce blocks, then transport the state via the IBC relayer. This “physics-level” gap makes the cross-chain experience extremely sluggish.

If being slow is tolerable, then the liquidation mechanism’s risk is basically a ticking time bomb. Aave V4 splits into two core components: Core Lending Spoke handles lending/borrowing, while the BTC Vault Swap Spoke is responsible for liquidation and settlement. In crypto markets,行情 often crashes like a waterfall. Once a drop triggers the liquidation line, the system also has to cross-chain to verify that time-consuming ZK proof. The timing gap caused by asynchronous settlement can be devastating. Many times, just when you see the liquidation warning, you don’t have time to transfer funds to top up collateral before it’s already gone—because the mainnet confirmation is still in the queue.

Babylon’s official documentation also doesn’t shy away from the fact that there is a “temporary trust gap” in the middle. Keeping funds on the original chain does prevent hackers from stealing them—but if the tradeoff is that it can blow up at any moment due to network latency, then the cost-effectiveness of this方案 really has to be discounted. The above is only my personal observations from testing, not investment advice. Do you think this kind of geek-romantic idea is worth risking real money? See you in the comments. #eth $ETH

@babylonlabs_io

No matter how nice Babylon’s “security as a service” sounds, when the technical integration doesn’t line up feature-wise, everything is for nothing.
$BTC #ETH 
Also, Babylon’s epoch mechanism determines the rhythm of cross-chain communication—each epoch is about 1 hour, and after it ends, the AppHash is packaged into the Bitcoin network. For a PoS chain to confirm state changes on the Babylon chain, it has to wait for the Bitcoin network to confirm that timestamp. This latency must be taken into account when designing cross-chain applications.
#baby $BABY 
In my view, cross-chain integration between Babylon and PoS chains is far more complex than people think. It’s not something you can solve just by opening a channel between two parties; you have to match feature lists, epoch timing, and trust period parameters chain by chain. Ecosystem expansion moves slowly—maybe it’s not only a matter of willingness, but also of technical complexity.

As for whether to fund (i.e., invest), that’s even more complicated. I’m always the first one to get scared; at least I got some testnet airdrops..

The pitch for this setup is pretty compelling: $BTC sits safely on the mainnet, and you avoid the hassle of cross-chain transfers, wrapping, and custody. During the challenge period for asynchronous settlement, if the network hiccups even slightly, you won’t have time to top up collateral. After I dug into Babylon’s ConsumerRegistryList interface, I found that some PoS chains have quietly been onboarded.

A while back, while studying Babylon’s API documentation, I came across an interface called ConsumerRegistryList. I assumed it was a normal list query, but the data returned made me stare at the screen for a long time—it was honestly pretty wild, really @babylonlabs_io 

The purpose of this interface is to query all the “consumer chains” that have already registered on Babylon—those PoS chains that have paid for Babylon’s security services. Each chain has its own name, description, and connection method, essentially a public “customer roster.”

The first question that popped into my head was: which chain is already using Babylon? $BABY 

Following the returned data, I noticed Babylon has already started onboarding Ethereum’s Layer 2 networks. It’s not a Cosmos ecosystem chain—it’s directly integrating with Ethereum’s Layer 2. This means Babylon’s ambition is much bigger than I imagined. It’s not just acting as security for Cosmos chains; its goal is to sell Bitcoin’s security capabilities to the entire blockchain world. #BTC #ETH 

I went back to look at the configuration definitions for this interface and found that the system assigns each onboarded consumer chain a unique identifier. In other words, Babylon has issued each integrated chain a kind of “ID number.”

At that point, I thought: if dozens of chains come over in the future and register, the data returned by this interface would turn into a real-time “Babylon security ecosystem leaderboard.” Developers who want to integrate with Babylon can check this interface first to see whose system is already running. This interface reveals Babylon’s actual expansion speed—more honestly than any marketing copy. #baby 

My takeaway can be summed up in one sentence: Babylon isn’t just discussing concepts—it’s building infrastructure. I used to think Babylon was just finding a PoS chain partner and sending tokens, but now it looks like it’s making a much bigger play—turning Bitcoin’s security capabilities into a wholesale business, selling to Ethereum’s Layer 2 networks, and also to Cosmos chains.

Of course, just because you can see who’s connected in the interface doesn’t necessarily mean they’re secure. But at the very least, it shows that the onboarding party is willing to hand its security to Babylon—and that, by itself, is a vote of trust. Check this interface again after a while and see whether the list gets longer. Whether the ecosystem expands or not is more real than Twitter.🎯

这个接口的作用是查询所有已经在Babylon上注册的“消费者链”——就是那些花钱买了Babylon安全服务的PoS链。每个链都有自己的名字、简介、接入方式，相当于一份公开的“客户名单”。

我当时脑子里冒出来的第一个问题是：到底哪条链已经在用Babylon了？$BABY 

顺着返回的数据往下看，我发现Babylon已经在接以太坊的二层网络了。不是Cosmos生态的链，是直接对接以太坊的Layer2。这意味着Babylon的野心比我想象的大得多——它不只是给Cosmos链当保安，它的目标是把比特币的安全能力卖给整个区块链世界。#BTC #ETH 

我又去翻了一下这个接口对应的配置定义，发现系统给每条接入的消费者链都分配了一个唯一的编号。也就是说，Babylon给每条接入的链都发了“身份证号”。

我当时就在想，如果未来几十条链都跑过来注册，这个接口返回的数据就会变成一份“Babylon安全生态的实时榜单”。开发者想接入Babylon，先去这个接口看一眼谁家已经在跑了。这个接口藏着Babylon生态的真实扩张速度，比任何宣传稿都诚实。#baby 

我的感受就一句话，Babylon不是在做概念，是在搭基础设施。 以前以为Babylon只是找个PoS链合作然后发币，现在看来它在下一盘更大的棋——把比特币的安全能力做成批发业务，卖给以太坊的二层网络，也卖给Cosmos链。

当然，接口里能看到谁接了，不代表接了就一定安全。但它至少说明，接入方愿意把安全交给Babylon，这本身就是一种信任投票。 等过段时间再去刷这个接口，看看列表有没有变长。生态扩不扩张，这里比推特更真实。🎯

Even more worrying is that Duel.com’s official X account has been suspended, yet its AML policy claims it enforces KYC and is compliant. Thorn said bluntly: if the platform still refuses to freeze funds after receiving a notice of stolen funds with forensics attached, then in essence it is assisting the theft.

Thorn is currently publicly pressuring people associated with the platform and warning that if the funds are not frozen, the platform will face major legal lawsuits.

The incident once again serves as a wake-up call to all hardware wallet users: private key security is only the first line of defense. Once funds leave your control, even with a complete forensics trail, cross-border recovery remains extremely difficult. Offshore gambling platforms are becoming a new breeding ground for money laundering and stolen-fund transit.

The old tricks in the market, when you strip them down, basically boil down to a “bait-and-switch”—lock the real big pie at home, then go to another network to create a mapped/representative coin. On the surface, it looks like it “activates” the liquidity pool, but at its core it infinitely magnifies security risks. You take the most robust asset with the whole network’s consensus, and tie it together with cross-chain bridges or multisig institutions that could blow up at any time—purely gambling with your life for hard-earned money.

But TBV’s logic is completely different: the principal is rock solid, and the cross-chain legwork is merely “proving” data.

The key to making the whole model work lies in an extremely clever technique: “single UTXO combined with Taproot preset signatures.” The main BTC chain is already pretty heavy; it has zero interest in parsing what those fancy PoS chains are doing with staking or liquidation. Its job is extremely simple and brutal: it only pays attention to the ZK data fed in externally, and checks whether this matches the withdrawal path (Spend Path) that was already hard-coded when the position was opened.

The impact of this mechanism is that it literally pulls the defense line back one layer to the most hardened BTC network. We no longer need to gamble on the conscience of third-party custodians; instead, we hand our life savings and life-or-death matters over to cold, unfeeling cryptography and script constraints. As long as you tightly hold your private key, that money will be as stable as a mountain.

Of course, even a beautiful lab model has to stand up to the abuse of real-world usage. When large sums move in and out in the future, that challenge window designed to prevent wrongdoing—just how sluggish will it make capital turnover? That’s something the real market environment will have to digest.

But one thing can be concluded: in the second half, the fight is already past the stage where people are fooled by issuing tokens that are backed by fake claims. title: Julho de 2026: o mês em que a cripto driblou o medo — e o que esperar de agosto
subTitle:
Fechamos mais um mês e, olhando o quadro geral, a leitura segue sendo a de um mercado fragilizado dentro do bear market, caminhando pra sua fase final. Mas segura esse sorriso de lado: mesmo com o ciclo se encerrando, ainda vamos passar por correções antes da próxima grande expansão. Julho foi um mês estranho — cheio de tensão, mas também de surpresas.
O pano de fundo: geopolítica e economia
Julho começou com uma trégua parcial entre Estados Unidos e Irã, com o Brent recuando pra perto de $71-72 depois de um trimestre de forte alta do petróleo. Só que a calma durou pouco: no meio do mês, os EUA revogaram autorizações de comércio com petróleo iraniano e retomaram ataques militares, levando o Brent de volta pra cima de $80. Na sequência, o conflito voltou a esquentar perto do Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb, chegando a ameaçar os $100 por barril antes de arrefecer de novo. Foi um mês de vai-e-volta constante no risco geopolítico.
No lado do Fed, a leitura mudou: o mercado tirou da mesa a ideia de um corte de juros esse ano e passou a precificar até mais uma alta em 2026, com o juro de 2 anos nos EUA perto de 4,2%. Ou seja, o pivô que muita gente esperava ficou mais distante.
Como a cripto reagiu
E aqui está o dado mais curioso do mês: mesmo com todo esse barulho macro, Bitcoin e Ethereum bateram todos os principais ativos do mercado. O #ETH  subiu cerca de 20% no mês, saindo de perto de $1.600 e fechando perto de $1.900-1.950. O #BTC  subiu cerca de 9%, saindo de perto de $60.000 (chegou a testar abaixo disso no início do mês) e fechando perto de $64-65 mil. Pra comparação: o Nasdaq 100 caiu cerca de 9% e as ações de semicondutores desabaram mais de 20% no mesmo período — a rotação de capital saiu de IA e parte foi pra cripto.
O detalhe mais importante: tudo isso aconteceu com o Fear & Greed Index travado em 28 ("Medo"). Ou seja, o preço subiu, mas o sentimento do mercado continuou desconfiado o mês inteiro — geralmente é esse tipo de descolamento entre preço e sentimento que caracteriza fundo de ciclo, não topo.
No institucional, o fluxo foi seletivo: BTC fechou o mês com entrada líquida de cerca de $172 milhões em ETFs (mesmo com saída forte no último dia), enquanto ETH liderou com $365 milhões em entradas, puxado pelo ETHB da BlackRock. Isso reforça que o capital institucional está migrando pra ETH, não saindo da cripto como um todo.
O capital especulativo, enquanto isso, migrou forte pra meme coins — historicamente esse comportamento marca a fase final da altseason e costuma anteceder uma sequência de correções. A semana também teve mais de $10 bilhões em liquidações, principalmente de posições compradas alavancadas — o mercado limpando quem estava exposto demais antes de definir a direção.
Moeda por moeda
$BTC  fechou dentro da região de ajuste que vínhamos monitorando. Abaixo dos $63 mil, os suportes ficam em $61 mil e depois $58 mil (suporte forte); num cenário de correção mais ampla, o próximo teste seria o fundo em $54 mil. Acima de $65-66 mil, o ativo entra numa região de pullback — a faixa mais importante pra observar uma possível retomada de força compradora no curto prazo, sem invalidar o viés de baixa principal.{spot}(BTCUSDT)$ETH  foi o destaque absoluto do mês, com a razão ETH/BTC rompendo um canal de baixa que durava meses — o primeiro sinal real de força relativa do ETH em 2026. O padrão técnico aponta um possível alvo perto de $2.150, com o suporte em $1.800 funcionando como linha de corte: perder essa região muda o cenário.{spot}(ETHUSDT)$BNB  teve um mês mais discreto em preço, fechando perto de $586, sustentando o suporte técnico entre $560-564. Mas o fundamento ficou mais forte: Binance fez seu maior queima trimestral da história em 17/07, removendo 1,62 milhão de BNB (cerca de $932 milhões) de circulação, reforçando o modelo deflacionário. Além disso, a T. Rowe Price lançou um ETF multi-cripto alocando 11% em BNB — sinal de demanda institucional nova entrando, mesmo com o preço andando de lado.{spot}(BNBUSDT)
Minha leitura pra agosto
Seguimos monitorando, porque agora o comportamento do fluxo importa mais do que qualquer movimento isolado de preço. E calma... agosto tem histórico estatisticamente fraco pro Bitcoin, então já chega testando a paciência de todo mundo. Minha expectativa é de continuidade da volatilidade: geopolítica no Oriente Médio ainda não está resolvida de verdade, e o Fed sem sinal de corte tira um suporte importante que o mercado vinha precificando.
Pontos-chave pra acompanhar: BTC segurando os $58 mil sem perder, ETH testando os $1.800 como suporte pro alvo de $2.150, e BNB defendendo os $560. 
Opinião pessoal, fins educacionais, não é recomendação de investimento.

【The market gave a signal, but have you really understood it?】

Last night before bed, I glanced at the chart—ETH hovered at 1868 for two hours, with volatility nearly at zero. This silence isn’t calm; it’s buildup.

When I was doing trade back then, I already knew that the dead quiet before a storm is the most unbearable—but also the most valuable.

Let me talk through my reasoning. This isn’t investment advice. Fights-with-words, step aside.

Now the market’s fear index is stuck at 27, and the weekly average is also 27. What does that number mean? I’ve been through three bull-and-bear cycles. Every time FNG drops into the 20–30 range, the market is full of complaints—everywhere you look, people are posting “zero-warning.” But when you look back, none of the ones who held spot at that level regretted it.

ETH is down 62% from its peak, and trading volume has withered—everyone seems to be lying flat and playing dead. Doesn’t that tell you something? The sellers who truly wanted out left early; what’s left either refuses to give up or is waiting for a reason.

From a business-logic perspective, I haven’t seen any fundamental destruction of ETH’s ecosystem. Layer 2 and DeFi infrastructure are still running. Being oversold doesn’t mean it will bounce immediately, but when it’s undervalued, building a position in batches has a much higher chance than chasing highs—that’s a lesson I verified back when I was doing e-commerce.

My plan: support at 1786. If it breaks, cut losses—no fantasies. Resistance at 1917. Once it breaks through, consider adding. Before the direction is clear, I’ll test with a light position and keep adjusting as it moves.

At this level, I’m not saying it must go up, but the odds have started to look favorable.

昨晚睡前瞄了眼盘面，ETH在1868横了两个小时，波动率几乎归零——这种沉默不是平静，是蓄力。

我做贸易那会儿就知道，暴风雨前的死寂最磨人，但也最值钱。

说说我的判断逻辑，不构成建议，杠精绕道。

现在市场恐惧指数卡在27，周均也是27，这个数字什么概念？我经历过三轮牛熊，每次FNG砸到20-30区间，市场骂声一片，朋友圈全是"归零警告"，但回头看，那个位置拿现货的，没一个后悔的。

ETH从高点跌了62%，成交量萎靡到大家都在躺平装死——这不就说明了什么？真正想卖的早跑了，剩下的要么死扛，要么在等一个理由。

#baby $BABY At midnight I was messing around and ended up going to @babylonlabs_io  to test the net experience of TBV. Right at the start it directly made me feel totally shut down—completely froze in place for a full quarter of an hour. The system kept forcing me to confirm two dozen-plus pre-signed transactions, clicking “confirm” until my wrists ached. At first I even wondered if the Fox wallet had crashed. Later, after carefully reading the technical notes, I finally understood: this is the unavoidable hurdle of BitVM3 garbled circuits. When creating a vault, you have to pre-sign every possible future withdrawal scenario, and firmly lock it into the Taproot script. It’s honestly torturous.

Right after that, I tested with 0.01 signet BTC. In the beginning it looked fine, but I immediately hit an extremely frustrating constraint: it forcibly requires a fixed denomination. The page only offers a few dead options—0.01, 0.1, and 1 BTC. I wanted to deposit 0.05, but the system simply said it doesn’t recognize it. The underlying logic is: once fan-out is greater than 1, the garbled circuit’s backward-pass will throw a bug. So each vault can only be a separate isolated island with a fixed amount. In plain terms, it’s hard-coded—turning a flexible “big pie” into rigid “meal tickets.” The way $BABY  is playing this, it’s really grinding flexibility into the ground.

This whole design is rigid to the extreme. For example, if later that big pie runs up to seventy thousand dollars, can I add a 0.02 position into the existing vault? No way—I’d have to pull money out and open a brand-new one. Want to merge two small vaults into one? Also impossible. As soon as the pre-signed transaction tree is generated, it becomes completely fixed. And once you factor in the extremely high Gas friction and waiting costs on the real mainnet, players with smaller funds will definitely be discouraged by this cumbersome process.

What’s even more ridiculous is the liveness assumption. The official pitch is loud and clear: it’s a 1-of-N mechanism, and as long as there’s at least one honest verifier watching over it, things will be fine. But who’s going to do that thankless job? I searched around on GitHub and couldn’t find any publicly available watchtower code. Ordinary retail users have neither the time nor the resources to set this up. In the end, the “fallback” is most likely Babylon internally, or some interested party. That’s not the same as the fully trustless model we think we’re getting. #baby

If we take WBTC—the widely known reference—as an example, even though its centralized model is constantly criticized, at least it’s free to enter and exit: you can move as much as you want.#eth $ETH
